prerequisites: Have passed, or be enrolled in, all subjects from previous years

learning_outcomes.text: Know the existing technology for the control and treatment of polluting gaseous emissions
Know the basic processes for water conditioning and wastewater treatment
Know the operation of wastewater treatment plants
Know the integrated process of industrial waste treatment
Know and be able to apply different industrial pollution prevention tools
Be able to analyze and evaluate the environmental impact of technical solutions

syllabus_topics: Introduction and definition of environmental technology.
Impacts of human activities on the environment.
Waste generation. Waste classification and coding.
Management of industrial waste. Industrial Waste Treatment Center (CTRI).
TEMA 4: Treatment of industrial and urban waters.
Characteristics of urban and industrial wastewater.
Urban and industrial wastewater treatment plants (WWTP).
Types and origin of atmospheric pollutants.
Dispersion of pollutants in the atmosphere.
Introduction to environmental impact assessment techniques.
Practice 1. Preparation of immobilized activated carbon for use as adsorbent.
Practice 2. Removal of pollutants by adsorption with immobilized activated carbon.
Practice 4. Simulation of a wastewater treatment plant (I).
Practice 5. Simulation of a wastewater treatment plant (II).
Practice 6: Life cycle analysis of a product.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practices reports, practicum and external internships

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade is based on laboratory practices (10%), case studies (20%), objective questions exams (30%), and a problem-solving exam (40%). To pass, students must complete laboratory practices and case studies, obtain a minimum of 5.0/10 in the average of objective questions exams, a minimum of 5.0/10 in the problem-solving exam, and achieve an overall weighted score of 5.0/10. For global assessment, students take an objective questions exam (50%) and a problem-solving and/or exercises exam (50%), requiring a minimum of 5.0/10 in each. In the second call, grades for laboratory practices and case studies are maintained, and students only retake unpassed exams, with the same passing criteria as the first call.
